extra.Backend: c:\Onee drive data\zenith 3\z-back-latest — Node, Express 4, Mongoose 8, Socket.IO 4, node-cron, Razorpay SDK, Puppeteer, AWS S3
extra.Frontend: c:\Onee drive data\zenith 3\z-front-v2 — React 18 (CRA + craco), React Router 6, Axios, TanStack Query, Radix/Tailwind, Capacitor 8 (Android)
extra.Database: MongoDB, single database, multi-tenant by company_id

nodes.name: Employee
nodes.description: Self-service portal user. Role `employee` on the User document; gated by company settings, plan feature and invitation acceptance before login succeeds.

nodes.name: Company admin
nodes.description: Role `admin`. Runs one tenant — employees, payroll, leave, attendance and billing for their own company only.

nodes.name: Super admin
nodes.description: Role `super_admin`. Platform operator. Provisions offline-billed companies, resolves seat requests, settles offline invoices. Seeded at boot by `ensureSuperAdmin`.

nodes.name: Prospect
nodes.description: Unauthenticated visitor on the public pricing and signup pages. Has no company or user record until signup creates them.

nodes.name: Razorpay API
nodes.description: Payment gateway. Holds the customer, the recurring subscription (plan times quantity), one-time orders for prorated charges, and the UPI or card mandate.

nodes.name: Razorpay Checkout
nodes.description: Browser-side `window.Razorpay` widget. On success it hands back a payment id and signature, which the client posts to a confirm endpoint.

nodes.name: AWS S3 and CloudFront
nodes.description: Object store for leave documents, reimbursement receipts, regularization attachments, employee documents and company logos. Reads are served as time-limited signed URLs.

nodes.name: emailService.sendEmail
nodes.description: Sends from the company's own configured mailbox, falling back to the shared platform mailbox. Bodies come from `utils/emailTemplate.renderEmail` plus company branding.

nodes.name: ZenithLanding
nodes.description: Public marketing page. Hosts the login dialog rather than routing to a login page.

nodes.name: Login
nodes.description: Modal opened from the landing page. Calls `login`, then `verifyOtp` when two-factor is required, and routes by role to /super-admin/dashboard, /dashboard or /employee/dashboard.

nodes.name: AuthProvider
nodes.description: Holds the user, the access token and the two-factor pending state. On Capacitor it persists user, token and refresh token in Preferences; on web it reads the `user` cookie and relies on the httpOnly refresh cookie.

nodes.name: axiosInstance
nodes.description: Single HTTP client. Attaches the bearer token and, on a 401, runs one shared refresh deduped through `refreshPromise` before replaying the queued requests. A failed refresh latches `refreshFailed` and surfaces the session-expired modal.

nodes.name: SubscriptionProvider
nodes.description: Caches the plan feature map from the features endpoint, plus plan name and id, raw status, `isPaidOnline` and any soft warning.

nodes.name: RoleAccessProvider
nodes.description: Caches the per-feature action grid from the permissions endpoint and exposes `can(feature, action)`.

nodes.name: WebSocketProvider
nodes.description: Socket.IO client. Listens for `new_notification` and exposes joinRoom, leaveRoom and subscribe so a page can follow a server-side job room instead of polling.

nodes.name: ProtectedRoute
nodes.description: Redirects unauthenticated users, enforces `requireRole`, and checks the route's feature and actions against RoleAccessContext before rendering.

nodes.name: FeatureProtectedRoute
nodes.description: Gates a route on a subscription feature, with an optional alternative feature and a disallowed-plans list, sending admins to /subscription with the reason in router state.

nodes.name: initializeSocket
nodes.description: Socket.IO server attached to the same HTTP server before listen. Rooms are joined by name; `new_notification` is broadcast to all clients with the recipient ids inside the payload.

nodes.name: POST /api/auth/login
nodes.description: Unauthenticated. Takes email or username, password, and the Capacitor `Device` object.

nodes.name: login
nodes.description: Runs the full admission sequence — user exists, account active, invitation accepted, company active, subscription usable, employee status, portal enabled, portal feature on the plan — and only then compares the password.

nodes.name: two_factor_enabled or super_admin
nodes.description: Super-admins always get an OTP; other users only when `two_factor_enabled` is set. Everyone else is issued tokens straight away.

nodes.name: otpStore
nodes.description: Process-local in-memory map keyed by email, holding a six-digit OTP and a five-minute expiry. Not persisted and not shared between processes.

nodes.name: verifyOTP
nodes.description: Validates the OTP against otpStore, deletes it, then mints the same token pair the direct login path would have.

nodes.name: createAccessToken and createRefreshToken
nodes.description: The access token carries `sub` (email), role and company_id. On web the refresh token goes into an httpOnly cookie; on mobile it is returned in the body and stored in Capacitor Preferences.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.description: Accepts the refresh token from the cookie, the Authorization header or the body, requires the token type to be `refresh`, and returns a new access token only. It does not rotate the refresh token.

nodes.name: auth
nodes.description: Verifies the bearer token and loads the User by `payload.sub`, putting the whole document on `req.user`. Distinguishes an expired access token from an invalid one so the client knows when to refresh.

nodes.name: traceContext
nodes.description: Mounted app-wide, above the raw-body webhook route. Seeds an AsyncLocalStorage trace with a flow inferred from the path, honours an inbound request id, and echoes a trace id on the response.

nodes.name: notFound and errorHandler
nodes.description: Terminal Express error middleware. Logs through the trace logger, never leaks a 500 message, and returns the trace id so a user can quote one id in a support ticket.

nodes.name: requireActiveSubscription
nodes.description: Hard-blocks suspended, cancelled, expired and trial_expired; marks past_due and paused as a soft warning. It also patches `res.json` so every guarded response carries a subscription block.

nodes.name: requireSubscriptionFeature
nodes.description: Per-feature gate. Whole routers use it — reimbursements require `advanced_payroll`; performance, goals and templates require `performance_management`.

nodes.name: requireRole
nodes.description: Compares `req.user.role` against an allow-list. Applied unevenly; several super-admin routes still rely on the client not rendering the page instead.

nodes.name: hasSubscriptionFeature
nodes.description: Resolves the company's current plan id from the subscription collection rather than the denormalised Company snapshot, then reads the flag off the plan's feature map. Returns false on any error instead of throwing.

nodes.name: GET /api/subscription-plans/role/permissions
nodes.description: Served with no-store cache headers so a permission change is never masked by a cached response.

nodes.name: SubscriptionPlan
nodes.description: Global plan catalogue — one document per plan, shared by every tenant on it. Its `features` map, including `employee_limit`, is what every feature gate reads.

nodes.name: User
nodes.description: Login identity — email, passwordHash, role, company_id, optional employee_id and access_role_id, and the invitation sent/accepted flags.

nodes.name: Company
nodes.description: Tenant root. Carries a denormalised `subscription_info` snapshot kept in step with CompanySubscription whenever seats change.

nodes.name: CompanySettings
nodes.description: One document per company holding leave_config, shifts, work_locations, rating_config, reimbursement_config, accessRoles, holidays, bank accounts, departments, designations and `employee_portal_enabled`.

nodes.name: Employee
nodes.description: HR record — salary_structure, leave_balance, activeShift, manager_id, rating, status (active, exit_scheduled, resigned, terminated) and termination_id.

nodes.name: Invitation
nodes.description: One-time activation token per email and company, with an expiry and an accepted flag. Re-issuing renews the same row rather than creating a second one.

nodes.name: LoginHistory
nodes.description: One row per employee sign-in, with IP, parsed device name and IP-derived location. Backs the admin Login Details page.

nodes.name: MonthlyActivityLog
nodes.description: Append-only audit trail behind the Activity Logs page, written by `addLog`.

nodes.name: addLog
nodes.description: Records a company-scoped audit entry — actor kind, action and message.

nodes.name: createNotification
nodes.description: Writes one Notification for a named recipient and emits `new_notification` over Socket.IO.

nodes.name: createAdminNotification
nodes.description: Resolves every admin User in the company, writes one Notification addressed to all of them, then emits over Socket.IO. A socket failure is warned about, never thrown — cron runs have no socket.

nodes.name: createSuperAdminNotification
nodes.description: Platform-level notification for events that belong to no tenant. Never throws.

nodes.name: EmployeeList
nodes.description: Roster, and the entry point to both seat top-up paths — it branches on `isPaidOnline` between the self-serve purchase flow and the seat-request queue.

nodes.name: createEmployee
nodes.description: Enforces the seat limit, strips department fields when that paid feature is off, rejects duplicate employee ids and emails, creates the Employee and its User, seeds leave balances and the attendance document, then issues the portal invite.

nodes.name: checkEmployeeLimit
nodes.description: Two gates. First the plan's hard `employee_limit` cap, which only a plan upgrade can lift; then the licensed seat count `number_of_employees`, which an add-on or a super-admin grant can raise. A limit of -1 means unlimited.

nodes.name: assignLeaveBalanceForEmployee
nodes.description: Turns the company's leave_config into the new employee's opening `leave_balance` rows.

nodes.name: sendEmployeePortalInvite
nodes.description: Renews or creates an Invitation with a fresh uuid token and an expiry, builds the activation link from FRONTEND_URL, and sends it through the company mailbox. Throws if the send fails.

nodes.name: AcceptEmployeeInvitation
nodes.description: Also serves /accept-admin-access for admin access-role invitations.

nodes.name: verifyEmployeeInvite
nodes.description: Rejects an unknown, already-accepted or expired token, and confirms a matching User exists before returning the company name and role to render the form.

nodes.name: acceptEmployeeInvite
nodes.description: Sets the password hash on the existing User, flips `is_invitation_accepted`, and marks the Invitation accepted.

nodes.name: createNewAttendance
nodes.description: Creates the month's EmployeeAttendance document. Called with `manual` for one new hire and with `auto` by the first-of-month cron for everyone.

nodes.name: EmployeeLeave
nodes.description: Balances, history, the apply dialog and the leave-encashment request form.

nodes.name: ApplyLeaveDialog (LeaveRequestDialog)
nodes.description: Computes the day count client-side and hands the form, the days and the optional document to its `onSubmit` prop; the page posts it as multipart FormData.

nodes.name: POST /api/leaves/leave-request
nodes.description: Multipart, single `document` field. The optional `:id` is the admin-on-behalf form; without it the employee comes from the token.

nodes.name: createLeaveRequest
nodes.description: Validates the half-day window and the date order, resolves the leave type out of company leave_config, refuses unpaid types, checks for an overlapping pending or approved request, and only then uploads the document and writes the row as pending.

nodes.name: LeaveRequest
nodes.description: One row per request — dates, days, half-day window, status (pending, approved, rejected, cancelled), the document key, and the approver, rejecter and canceller audit fields.

nodes.name: LeaveManagement
nodes.description: Admin queue. Approve or reject, apply on behalf, cancel, edit an approved leave, and resolve encashment requests.

nodes.name: approveOrRejectLeaveRequest
nodes.description: Refuses anything already finalised, then claims the row with a findOneAndUpdate scoped to `status: "pending"` so a second click loses the race. On approval it deducts the balance, reconciles the attendance days, paints the leave onto the schedule, and auto-cancels other pending requests overlapping the same dates.

nodes.name: reconcileApprovedLeaveDates
nodes.description: For each date in the range, removes the system-generated unpaid-leave fallback that a missed punch had created, so an approved leave does not sit on top of a system absence.

nodes.name: updateLeaveSchedule
nodes.description: Writes the approved leave across the attendance days it covers, honouring the half-day window.

nodes.name: EmployeeDashboard
nodes.description: Carries the punch-in and punch-out controls. Sends the client's own clock time, the timezone offset, the Capacitor device info and, when geofencing is on, the coordinates.

nodes.name: recordTodayAttendance
nodes.description: Finds or creates the month's attendance document and today's day entry, stamps the client-supplied time, evaluates lateness against the assigned shift's grace period, and on an early punch-out downgrades the day to an unpaid half-day.

nodes.name: CheckLoginGeoSphere
nodes.description: Compares the punch coordinates against the company's work locations. Only consulted when `isCheckinOutEnabled` is set on company settings.

nodes.name: EmployeeAttendance
nodes.description: One document per employee per month holding a `days` array — status, punch_in, punch_out, work_duration_minutes, late_by_minutes, early_leave_minutes, leave_id, is_lop and a shift snapshot.

nodes.name: LateArrival
nodes.description: One row per exception day — `late_arrival`, `early_punch_out` or `missed_punch_in` — plus the embedded `regularization` sub-document that carries the request through review.

nodes.name: EmployeeAttendance
nodes.description: Calendar view. Opens the regularization form on a late, absent or early-punch-out day and sends the specific LateArrival id so a day carrying two records targets the right one.

nodes.name: POST /api/attendance/regularization-requests
nodes.description: Multipart, single `attachment` field.

nodes.name: createRegularizationRequests
nodes.description: Matches the whole local calendar day when hunting for the LateArrival, because punch-flow records are stored at server-local midnight while missed-punch records use UTC midnight. Where no record exists it synthesises one, but only for an absent day or a late punch-in day.

nodes.name: updateRegularizationRequests
nodes.description: Refuses an already-processed request, stamps the decision onto the embedded regularization, and on approval dispatches to the handler matching the record's event type.

nodes.name: handleLateArrivalApproval, handleEarlyPunchOutApproval, handleMissedPunchInApproval
nodes.description: The three attendance corrections. Approving an early punch-out restores the day from an unpaid half-day; approving a missed punch rebuilds the day from the times the employee supplied.

nodes.name: RunPayroll
nodes.description: Tab shell over the regular, termination, one-time and history payroll views.

nodes.name: RegularPayroll
nodes.description: Drives the whole run — generate, edit and save a draft row, lock the selected employees, then complete.

nodes.name: getPayrollCalculationData
nodes.description: Computes the whole month and persists it as a draft run. Basic-payroll companies take a hard-return short path that only sums the salary structure; advanced payroll additionally needs a tax config and prorates by attendance, promotions and overtime.

nodes.name: calculateStatutoryDeductions
nodes.description: EPF, ESI, professional tax and LWF, using the company tax config plus the bundled `professional_tax_slabs.json` and `lwf.json`.

nodes.name: calculateTDS
nodes.description: Progressive slab tax over the projected annual taxable income.

nodes.name: buildSalarySegments
nodes.description: Splits the month wherever a promotion takes effect and prorates each segment, so a mid-month raise is paid at both rates.

nodes.name: OTLog
nodes.description: Approved overtime hours. Only read when the company's payroll settings enable overtime.

nodes.name: PayrollRun
nodes.description: One document per company, period and type (regular, termination, one-time), holding the per-employee computed rows. Status moves draft, locked, completed. `applied_loans` and `loan_repayments_recorded` are what make deleting a run reversible.

nodes.name: lockPayrollRun
nodes.description: Keeps only the employees the admin selected, merging their edited figures by employee id rather than by array position, and sets the run to locked.

nodes.name: completePayroll
nodes.description: Refuses a run that is not locked. Applies each loan EMI and records the amount actually taken, marks the included reimbursement claims paid but only on advanced payroll, settles a termination run's exit record, then sets the run to completed and notifies every employee.

nodes.name: Loan
nodes.description: Employee loan with tenure, EMI, outstanding_amount, paid_emis and remaining_emis. Status runs pending, approved, disbursed.

nodes.name: Payslips
nodes.description: Selects payslips, uploads their rendered HTML, then polls the job until it finishes.

nodes.name: POST /api/payroll/payslips/email-with-pdfs
nodes.description: Multipart — an array of `pdfs` plus a JSON `selections` string that is the source of truth for who gets what.

nodes.name: emailPayslipsWithPdfs
nodes.description: Validates that the file count matches the selections, spills each upload to a per-job temp directory, writes the job row, and schedules it. It returns as soon as the job is queued.

nodes.name: PayslipEmailJob
nodes.description: Queue row with per-item status and the running processed, successful and failed counters. Its persistence is what lets the job survive a restart.

nodes.name: processPayslipEmailJob
nodes.description: In-process worker started via setImmediate, guarded by an `activePayslipEmailJobs` set so a job is never run twice concurrently. Three workers drain the item queue, pushing progress after every item.

nodes.name: renderHtmlToPdf and wrapPayslipHtml
nodes.description: Renders the uploaded payslip HTML to a PDF with puppeteer-core on the server, so client devices never have to.

nodes.name: GET /api/payroll/payslips/email-jobs/:jobId
nodes.description: Scoped to the caller's company; a job belonging to another tenant reads as not found.

nodes.name: resumePendingPayslipEmailJobs
nodes.description: Called from `server.js` before listen. Re-schedules every job still queued or processing, so a deploy mid-send does not strand it.

nodes.name: EmployeeTermination
nodes.description: Exit record — exit type, last working day, settlement date, exit-interview status, the linked payroll run, and a status that ends at `settled`.

nodes.name: EmployeeLoans
nodes.description: Employee-side loans and reimbursement claims in one screen.

nodes.name: POST /api/reimbursements
nodes.description: The whole router sits behind auth, an active subscription and the `advanced_payroll` feature.

nodes.name: applyReimbursement
nodes.description: Blocks a claim from an employee whose exit is in progress, enforces the company's claim window against the expense date, requires at least one receipt, and deletes every uploaded S3 key again if any upload or the insert fails.

nodes.name: ReimbursementRequest
nodes.description: Claim with receipts, approved_amount, remaining_amount, the payouts array and the pay period it was settled in. Status runs submitted, then approved or rejected, then paid.

nodes.name: changeReimbursementStatus
nodes.description: Only a submitted claim can be reviewed. Approving records an approved amount that may be lower than the claim, and sets remaining_amount to it so payroll knows what is still owed.

nodes.name: applyLoan
nodes.description: Writes the loan with outstanding_amount seeded from the total payable. Notifies admins only when the employee applied for themselves, not when an admin filed it on their behalf.

nodes.name: changeLoanRequestStatus
nodes.description: Approving seeds remaining_emis from the tenure; disbursing sets both disbursed_amount and outstanding_amount. Each transition writes an audit log and notifies the employee.

nodes.name: Performance Dashboard
nodes.description: Review queue across the company. Also drives bulk assignment, reminders, cancellation and deletion.

nodes.name: OneTimeReviewDialog
nodes.description: Assigns a single appraisal from a template, with a review name and an optional deadline.

nodes.name: POST /api/performance/appraisals/assign
nodes.description: The whole performance router requires the `performance_management` feature, which is forced on for `enterprise-plan` when a plan payload is normalised.

nodes.name: assignAppraisal
nodes.description: Requires an active or exit_scheduled employee and a company-owned Appraisal template, refuses a duplicate active review with the same name, defaults the deadline to 14 days out, creates the review at `Self Review` and bumps the template's usage count.

nodes.name: Template
nodes.description: Company-owned question sets, typed Appraisal, PIP or Exit Interview, with a `usedIn` counter.

nodes.name: EmployeeReview
nodes.description: One row per assigned review of any type. Carries the self_review, manager_review, employee_comments and exit-interview sub-documents, and a status that walks Self Review, Approval Review, Employee Comment, Admin Review, Completed.

nodes.name: EmployeeReviews
nodes.description: The employee's own appraisals, PIPs, exit interviews and goals in one list.

nodes.name: EmployeeAppraisalEditor
nodes.description: Submits the `self` review, and later the `employee` acknowledgement. Chosen by AppraisalEditorRouter when the signed-in role is employee.

nodes.name: ManagerAppraisalEditor
nodes.description: Submits the `manager` review, then `complete` to close the appraisal.

nodes.name: submitAppraisalReview
nodes.description: One handler for all four stages. `REVIEW_CONFIG` decides which current statuses are allowed in and which status the review moves to, and the caller must be the assigned employee, the assigned manager, or the default admin for the completing step.

nodes.name: sendAppraisalNotification
nodes.description: Looks the new status up in `STATUS_NOTIFICATION_CONFIG` and notifies whichever party that stage names — employee, manager or admin.

nodes.name: GoalTracking
nodes.description: Creates goals with their key results and updates key-result progress.

nodes.name: createGoal
nodes.description: Requires at least one key result, refuses a duplicate title while an earlier goal with that title is not Completed, and derives progress and status from the key results rather than trusting the client.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.description: OKR-style goal with keyResults, a derived progress percentage and a derived status.

nodes.name: EmployeeGoalView
nodes.description: Read-only detail of one goal, loaded by id.

nodes.name: updateGoalProgress
nodes.description: Recomputes progress and status from the submitted key results.

nodes.name: SignupPage
nodes.description: Collects the company, the admin and the seat count, calls the signup endpoint, opens Razorpay Checkout on the returned subscription, then posts the confirm callback.

nodes.name: POST /api/subscription-plans/payment/signupSubscription
nodes.description: Unauthenticated by necessity — the company and the user do not exist yet.

nodes.name: createSignupSubscription
nodes.description: Two branches. `free-trial` creates everything immediately, activates a 14-day trial and returns tokens. A paid plan creates the company as `pending`, creates an inactive admin user, computes per-user GST, creates the Razorpay subscription and a `created` Payment, and grants nothing until payment confirms.

nodes.name: provisionNewCompany
nodes.description: Seeds a new tenant — company settings, the state tax config, default leave types and the default admin access role.

nodes.name: Payment
nodes.description: Every charge, online or offline. Carries the Razorpay order, subscription and payment ids, the purpose, the method details, and `activation_confirmed` and `activation_source`, which are what keep the browser callback and the webhook from both activating.

nodes.name: CompanySubscription
nodes.description: The billing source of truth per company — plan, cycle, `number_of_employees` (licensed seats, and the Razorpay quantity), status, next_billing_date, `is_effective`, and `pending_mandate` while a replacement mandate awaits authorization.

nodes.name: POST /api/subscription-plans/payment/confirmAndActivate
nodes.description: Unauthenticated. The Razorpay signature is the only thing proving the caller completed this payment.

nodes.name: confirmPaymentAndActivate
nodes.description: Verifies HMAC of payment_id and subscription_id, re-fetches the payment from Razorpay rather than trusting the client, requires it to be captured, allows at most one rupee of drift per seat against the quote, checks the payment belongs to the recorded subscription, then activates.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/razorpay
nodes.description: Mounted directly on the app with `express.raw` BEFORE `express.json`, because the signature HMACs the raw body. `routes/razorpay.routes.js` documents at length why a duplicate JSON-parsed registration must never be re-added.

nodes.name: handleRazorpayWebhook
nodes.description: Verifies the signature, resumes the originating trace from `notes.trace_id`, then claims the event id in WebhookEvent — the unique index makes the claim atomic, so concurrent duplicates race on the insert. A handler that throws releases the claim so a Razorpay retry can reprocess.

nodes.name: WebhookEvent
nodes.description: The idempotency ledger. One row per Razorpay event id, with a unique index and a 30-day TTL.

nodes.name: onSubscriptionActivated
nodes.description: Finds the paid Payment for the subscription, short-circuits when activation is already confirmed, cancels the old subscription only for renewal and trial-to-paid flows, then creates the CompanySubscription and emails the receipt. A mandate-migration subscription is finalised instead and never falls through here.

nodes.name: onOrderPaid
nodes.description: The primary path for one-time charges. Routes on `notes.purpose` to the plan-upgrade applier or the seat add-on applier; an unknown order finds no pending request and no-ops.

nodes.name: createCompanySubscription
nodes.description: Writes the effective CompanySubscription from the plan, the Razorpay subscription and the payment.

nodes.name: UpgradePlan
nodes.description: One screen for seat add-ons, plan upgrades, cycle switches and renewals. It opens Checkout on whatever the server returned and then posts the matching confirm call.

nodes.name: POST /api/subscription-plans/employees/quote
nodes.description: Read-only. The company is taken from the token, never the body; only `extra_employees` is accepted from the client.

nodes.name: computeEmployeeProration
nodes.description: Prices the seats for the remainder of the current cycle and adds GST. The result is the only figure the order is ever created for.

nodes.name: purchaseEmployeeAddOn
nodes.description: Stages the request and creates the Razorpay order. Grants nothing. A partial unique index allows one pending request per company, so a concurrent second purchase loses on the insert.

nodes.name: EmployeeAddOnRequest
nodes.description: One staged seat purchase — seats before and after, the quoted amounts, the order id, and a status of pending_payment, applied or failed.

nodes.name: confirmSeatAddOn
nodes.description: Scopes the order to the caller's company, verifies the order-and-payment HMAC with a timing-safe compare, re-fetches the payment from Razorpay, and only then calls the shared applier — so it is safe to race the webhook.

nodes.name: applyPaidEmployeeAddOn
nodes.description: The convergence point. Validates before claiming, then claims the request with a compare-and-swap so exactly one entry point wins. Raises the Razorpay quantity at cycle end BEFORE granting seats locally, so seats are never licensed that cannot be billed; if the grant then fails, the claim is released.

nodes.name: createReplacementSubscription
nodes.description: The UPI fallback. Creates a new Razorpay subscription starting at the next billing boundary, cancelling any earlier unauthorized replacement first so an orphan cannot double-bill. Until the customer authorizes it, every update on the old one is rejected.

nodes.name: finalizeMandateMigration
nodes.description: On authorization, cancels the old subscription and points the local document at the new one. Idempotent — a second call finds no matching pending_mandate and no-ops. Reached from two webhooks and from the browser callback.

nodes.name: calculateUpgradeCostInternal
nodes.description: Classifies the change — prorated_upgrade, cycle_switch, renewal_full_charge, signup_full_charge — and prices it. The same function backs the quote the dialog shows and the order actually raised.

nodes.name: createUpgradeSubscription
nodes.description: Refuses anything that is not a prorated upgrade or a cycle switch, refuses an ended term twice over, and refuses an offline-billed company. A same-plan seat increase is redirected into the seat add-on order path.

nodes.name: PlanUpgradeRequest
nodes.description: One staged plan change — from and to plan, seats after, the cycle-switch flag, the target Razorpay plan id, the order id and the applied status.

nodes.name: confirmPlanUpgrade
nodes.description: Same shape as the seat confirm — a company-scoped lookup, a timing-safe signature compare, a gateway re-fetch, then the shared applier.

nodes.name: applyPaidPlanUpgrade
nodes.description: Claims the PlanUpgradeRequest with a compare-and-swap and runs the switch, so the webhook and the browser callback converge safely.

nodes.name: performPlanSwitch
nodes.description: Keeps the existing term and moves the plan fields. Refuses an ended term outright. A monthly-to-annual switch cancels the old subscription and stages an annual replacement instead; a plan change beyond the mandate's limit stages a replacement rather than failing.

nodes.name: BillingTrace
nodes.description: Scoped event log for subscription and payment flows only. A 500 on an unrelated route is deliberately dropped by the scope guard rather than polluting it.

nodes.name: utils/trace
nodes.description: Trace context, module loggers, spans and the named EVENTS and FLOWS constants. Persists the events that matter to BillingTrace and drains buffered events on an uncaught exception.

nodes.name: CompanyDetails
nodes.description: One company's full picture — resolve a seat request, provision seats or a plan directly, add an offline purchase, settle a payment, and read the billing trace.

nodes.name: createSeatRequest
nodes.description: Snapshots the true server-side seat state, refuses a request that would cross the plan cap because that needs an upgrade rather than a top-up, and relies on a partial unique index to allow one pending request per company.

nodes.name: SeatRequest
nodes.description: Also used as the audit row for a direct super-admin provision, which is written already resolved so the same timeline renders both paths identically.

nodes.name: resolveSeatRequest
nodes.description: Rejecting works for any company; approving is offline-only, guarded server-side because approving for an online company would license seats the Razorpay mandate never bills for. The super-admin may override the approved seat count.

nodes.name: POST /api/super-admin/companies/:companyId/provision
nodes.description: A `/provision/quote` sibling runs the same path and stops before the first write, so the figure the dialog shows is the figure invoiced.

nodes.name: provisionOfflineCompany
nodes.description: Grants seats or a plan change with no request to approve, checks the super_admin role in the handler itself, writes an already-resolved SeatRequest as the audit row, raises the invoice, and tells the company what changed.

nodes.name: applySeatsAndPlan
nodes.description: The single mutation point for seats, plan, cycle and custom rate, shared by the direct provision and the seat-request approval so the two paths cannot drift.

nodes.name: recordOfflineProvisionCharge
nodes.description: Raises the pending offline invoice for what was just granted. Never throws — a failure here must not undo the grant. It declines to invoice an online company.

nodes.name: PATCH settle offline payment
nodes.description: One of the few routes that enforces `requireRole("super_admin")` server-side, because it moves money-state on nothing but the caller's word.

nodes.name: settleOfflinePayment
nodes.description: Scoped to the company in the route, refuses a forward-dated paid_on, and refuses any payment not marked `notes.offline` — a gateway charge's status belongs to Razorpay, not to a click here.

nodes.name: utils/cron-jobs
nodes.description: Registered by requiring the module at the top of app.js. Billing jobs are wrapped in `tracedJob`, which gives each run its own root trace and swallows the failure so the next run still happens.

nodes.name: expireStaleMandateMigrations
nodes.description: Cancels replacement mandates whose start date passed unauthorized. The old subscription was never cancelled, so billing simply continued at the old rate.

nodes.name: expirePaidSubscriptions
nodes.description: Runs after the Razorpay sync so a mandate that renewed overnight cannot be graced by mistake. Moves ended manual terms into the grace window, then out of it.

nodes.name: processScheduledEmployeeExits
nodes.description: Finds employees whose last working date is today, moves them to resigned or terminated depending on the termination type, and deactivates their User in the same bulk write.
